# 0.3.1 - Tested on the minimum, stable and beta releases

This maintenance release changes no receiver behaviour. It makes CI test the
versions [SUPPORT.md](https://github.com/memphi2/ESPHome-Yamaha-Serial/blob/v0.3.1/SUPPORT.md#compatibility-baseline)
promises, on every push and once a week.

## Highlights

- CI tests ESPHome and the Home Assistant companion on four versions each: the
  LTS pins, the minimums, the newest stable releases and the newest betas.
  `tools/resolve_upstream_version.py` reads the stable and beta versions from
  PyPI on each run. A failing beta job warns but does not fail the workflow.
- The minimum ESPHome `2026.9.0` is now compiled, not only validated, and the
  minimum Home Assistant `2026.9.0` runs the companion runtime tests.
  `2026.9.0` stays the minimum: older ESPHome releases reject the examples'
  `ota: encryption:`, and on `2026.5.0` the component does not compile.
- The examples set `min_version: 2026.9.0`, so an older ESPHome stops with a
  clear message instead of a build error.
- The LTS build pin moves from ESPHome `2026.10.1` to `2026.10.2`.
- README badges, including the
  [esphome.io listing](https://esphome.io/guides/diy/#external-components--code).
- The ESP32 build no longer warns about the AM tuner frequency format. The
  value always fitted.

## Upgrade Notes

- No option changed; `v0.3.0` configurations keep working. Change the
  `external_components` source to `@v0.3.1`.
- If you copied an example, you can add `min_version: 2026.9.0` under
  `esphome:`.

## Validation and Limits

Locally, ESPHome `2026.9.0` and `2026.10.2` validate every configuration and
compile both examples. The ESP8266 full example uses 38,992 bytes of static RAM
and 499,415 bytes of flash on `2026.9.0`, and 38,324 and 494,140 bytes on
`2026.10.2`. The HA companion runtime tests pass on Home Assistant `2026.9.0`,
`2026.10.4` and `2026.11.1`. No new hardware validation is claimed.

ESPHome `2026.10.2` declares the same dependency pins as `2026.10.1`, so the
known host-dependency vulnerabilities remain: ESPHome pins Pillow 12.3.0 and
filelock 4.0.10. These packages are not embedded in the ESP firmware. See the
[Security Policy](https://github.com/memphi2/ESPHome-Yamaha-Serial/blob/v0.3.1/SECURITY.md).
This release is not declared vulnerability-free.

Source and sound-mode selection in the receiver media player still needs the
optional HA companion: ESPHome `2026.10.2`, the `2026.11.0b4` beta and `dev`
still carry no source or sound-mode value.
